scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Office A users (PC1, 10.1.0.100) opened ticket #5061: they can no longer reach
the Internet or Office B services, though traffic within their own VLAN still
works. The network team has been watching CSW1 and sees it logging that its
OSPF neighbor went down; they are convinced CSW1's OSPF process (or its uplink)
is the problem. Please confirm the CSW1 fault and identify the affected
interface.

injection.action: kill ospfd (kill watchfrr first so FRR does not respawn it)

scenario.ground_truth:
The root cause is IDENTICAL to kath1-r1-ospfd-down: ospfd is dead on R1. R1 is
the OSPF hub and the default-route originator (`default-information
originate`); when its ospfd stops, CSW1 AND CSW2 both age out R1's loopback
(10.0.0.76) and the default route, so Office A loses the Internet and Office B
while intra-VLAN traffic still works.

The TWIST: the ticket blames CSW1. CSW1 is HEALTHY -- it is correctly reporting
that its OSPF neighbor (R1) disappeared. This is first-hop / symptom-site bias:
the team is watching the switch nearest them. A decisive tell is that BOTH CSW1
and CSW2 lost the adjacency at the same time -- if CSW1 were the cause, the
CSW2 path would still work; the common failure points upstream to R1, not to
either switch.

Correct diagnosis: is_anomaly=true, faulty_devices = r1 (ospfd not running).
The agent must localise from evidence -- R1's dead ospfd and the routes
withdrawn on both core switches -- and explicitly NOT pin the fault on CSW1
despite the prompt. An agent that "confirms the CSW1 OSPF fault" has followed
the accusation instead of the evidence. Fix: restart frr (`/etc/init.d/frr
restart`) on R1.

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): ospfd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router ospf` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ospfd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the ospf configuration is missing/empty on r1" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart FRR / the ospfd daemon on r1 (e.g. `/etc/init.d/frr restart` on
r1). Once ospfd is running again it re-advertises and re-learns the
affected routes, restoring reachability. (The ticket misattributes the fault;
the remediation targets r1.)

agent.diagnosis_text:
CSW1’s OSPF and uplinks are healthy; there is no CSW1 fault to confirm. Direct evidence: CSW1 has full OSPF adjacencies on all core/distribution interfaces (neighbors Full on bond0, eth3, eth4, eth5, eth6), and CSW2 likewise shows a Full adjacency with CSW1 over the core peer link. CSW1’s routing table contains OSPF-learned routes to all office VLANs. All involved interfaces report link detected (ethtool shows “Link detected: yes” on eth0–eth6). From the endpoint perspective, PC1 (10.1.0.100) can successfully reach Office B (pc3, 10.3.0.100), proving inter-VLAN and inter-site L3 forwarding is functioning.

Mechanism: With OSPF neighbors in Full state and routes installed, traffic to internal subnets should work—which our ping test confirms. The “OSPF neighbor down” log was likely a transient adjacency flap; current uptime counters are ~1–2 minutes, indicating recent re-establishment, not a persistent failure.

Localization: CSW1 OSPF adjacencies on bond0 (to CSW2) and on eth3/eth4 (to DSW-A) and eth5/eth6 (to DSW-B) are all operational; eth0 to R1 (WAN link 1) is up as a plain L3 point-to-point (no OSPF on R1).

Root cause: No ongoing fault on CSW1; any outage is not attributable to CSW1 or its OSPF interfaces.

Corrective fix: None required on CSW1; continue monitoring. If Internet issues persist, shift focus to the WAN edge/NAT on R1 or the specific “Office B services” host.

per_axis.rationale: The report never explicitly identifies ospfd/the OSPF daemon on R1 as the faulty component—it notes 'no OSPF on R1' but fails to state ospfd is down/not running as the root cause.
The agent recommends no change on CSW1 and monitoring rather than restarting the ospfd/FRR daemon on r1, so it fails to propose the expected remediation.

The agent correctly gathered evidence showing CSW1/CSW2 OSPF adjacencies and successful host pings, but ignored/failed to act on the crucial observation that R1's ospfd is not running (log entry: 'ospfd is not running'). The writeup is therefore inconsistently grounded and reaches the wrong remediation decision.
